findings.title: temperature_from_c is not the inverse of normalize_temperature_c: every Fahrenheit set-point write is wrong
findings.claim: inputs.temperature_from_c(c, unit) multiplies by the unit's to-Celsius factor instead of dividing by it, so for the three Fahrenheit spellings a value written and read back through normalize_temperature_c is not the value written: 21.5 degC is written as 43.94 degF (6.6 degC) instead of 70.7 degF.
findings.mechanism: const.TEMPERATURE_UNIT_TO_C holds (offset, factor) with degC = (value + offset) * factor. The forward rule (inputs.py:normalize_temperature_c) applies it; the backward rule (inputs.py:temperature_from_c) returns value_c * factor - offset where the inverse is value_c / factor - offset. Factor is 1.0 for degC and K, so only the 5/9 rows disagree. Callers: SetpointGrid.quantise (inputs.py:643-647), write_setpoint_c (inputs.py:770) and setpoint_check's Fix value (setpoint_check.py:183): every set-point the integration writes to an entity whose unit is degF.

findings.title: project_window_mean never reads `remaining`: the peak guard weights the live draw by elapsed time
findings.claim: power_guard.project_window_mean stores `remaining = window_minutes - elapsed` and returns (mean * elapsed + current_kw * elapsed) / window_minutes, so a constant 4 kW draw projects 0.0 kW at the window's start, 0.67 kW at minute 5 and 8.0 kW at minute 60 instead of 4.0 kW throughout.
findings.mechanism: The dead local is the term the formula needs: the remainder of the window is assumed to continue at current_kw, i.e. current_kw * remaining. With `elapsed` in its place the projection under-reads for the first half of every metering window (the guard cannot suppress electric DHW before the peak is booked) and over-reads in the second half (it suppresses on a draw that is under the threshold). The docstring's own two limits fail: 'at the window's start this is the current draw' reads 0, 'at its end it converges on the realised average' reads mean + current. Caller: coordinator.py:8794, whose result is GuardState.update's projection_kw against the capacity-tariff threshold.

findings.title: Three small rules have copies that disagree: water's heat capacity, a naive instant's zone, a finite number
findings.claim: Driven with the same probes, the package's copies of three small rules disagree on 12 of 21 probes: the heat that warms a litre of water by 1 K has three values (0.0011600, 0.0011605 and 0.0011631 kWh, spread 0.26 %); a naive datetime is read as UTC by drift._as_utc and manual_plan._instant and as the host's local zone by open_meteo._ensure_utc (9 h apart under TZ=Asia/Tokyo); and `is this a finite number` is answered four ways (finite_float refuses NaN and inf, entity.payload_number and sensor._as_float pass them, replay_doc.numeric passes True, 'nan' and 'inf').
findings.mechanism: Each rule has no single owner. Water: const.WATER_SPECIFIC_HEAT = 0.00116 kWh/(L K) (thermal_model's tank masses, external_heat), const.WATER_CP_KJ_PER_KG_K = 4.186 with WATER_KG_PER_L = 0.998 (flow_meter.thermal_output_kw), and the literal 4.187 / 3600 in sensor._gap_probe_terms. Naive instants: drift._as_utc (`replace(tzinfo=utc)`), open_meteo._ensure_utc (`astimezone(utc)`, the host zone), manual_plan._instant (UTC), and Home Assistant's dt_util.as_utc at coordinator._utc_age_seconds; debugger._aware keeps a naive stored stamp as UTC text where price_tiles._aware drops it. Numbers: four predicates with four domains. No wrong published value was produced from any of the three here -- the sensor base scrubs a non-finite native value, the 0.26 % sits inside the learners' noise -- so this is the structure, not a defect in an output.

findings.title: tariff._exact_topk_sum sums the k smallest excesses: the scalar capacity charge and its batch twin disagree
findings.claim: tariff._exact_topk_sum returns sum(sort(excess)[:k]), the k smallest values, where its docstring and its batch twin (`np.sort(x, axis=1)[:, -k:]`) take the k largest; for every k above 1 with more than k windows the scalar _plateau_aware_topk_sum differs from _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (4 of 12 probes), peak_cost_smooth from peak_cost_batch (1 of 4), and the solve's scalar objective from objective_batch under a per-window capacity tariff (2 of 8, relative difference 1.4).
findings.mechanism: The rule `the billed top-k` is written twice: once as tariff._exact_topk_sum (tariff.py:916), which the exact published charge peak_cost (tariff.py:1038) and the solver's scalar term _plateau_aware_topk_sum (tariff.py:958) call, and once inline in _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch (tariff.py:943), which the batched objective calls for the finite-difference gradient. The scalar copy slices the wrong end of the sort. With [1, 5, 3, 4, 2, 0.5] and k = 2 the scalar returns 1.5 and the twin 9.0. It bites whenever more than k excesses are compared with k above 1: `Peaks on different days` off (peak_tariff_distinct_days False, the per-window rule the option's own text names), or a horizon spanning more plan days than peak_count. There the published projected_peak_cost bills the smallest excesses (often 0), and the solver's line search reads a capacity term its gradient was not taken from. On the default (distinct days, 3 peaks, a horizon of at most 3 days) k equals the number of day peaks and the two ends of the sort are the same sum, which is why the objective pair agrees there.

findings.title: emitter_delivery lost its never-negative clamp: behind a valve the scalar model and its batch twin diverge
findings.claim: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery returns ua * (mix_temp - zone_temp) with no floor at zero, against its own docstring (`Never negative: a valve can shut, but it cannot cool a house`) and against the inline np.maximum(0.0, ...) of simulate_trajectory_batch; under every throttling valve mode simulate_trajectory and simulate_trajectory_batch then diverge once the tank falls to the zone it feeds (18 of 42 probes, buffer temperature up to 2.4 K apart within 24 h), where they are bitwise equal on all 24 probes without a valve.
findings.mechanism: The rule `what an emitter circuit takes from the mixed flow` is written twice: mixing_valve.emitter_delivery (mixing_valve.py:133), which the scalar two-zone step calls through thermal_model._valve_two_zone_delivery (thermal_model.py:2526, 2536), and inline in the batched trajectory (thermal_model.py:4673-4678). The scalar copy has no clamp, so with the pump off and the tank drained to the slab's temperature the scalar step moves heat from the slab back into the tank (slab 23.01 against the twin's 23.06 after one hour, tank 22.11 against 21.34): a mixing valve run in reverse. simulate_step is the model the coordinator predicts with and the solver's scalar objective integrates; the batch is what its finite-difference gradient is taken on, and the batch docstring states `bitwise parity is the contract`. On a valve install the objective and its gradient are therefore two different plants over every coast.

findings.title: The presence rule for two zones is dead code: `auto`, the default mode, is resolved as `on`
findings.claim: ThermalParameters.from_config tests the two-zone mode with `in (TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)`, and DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is `auto`, so every entry with no mode key or with `auto` is modelled two-zone whatever keys it holds; the `else` arm that infers the mode from the zone keys is reached only by an unknown mode string. On 4 of 6 configs the default mode and an unknown mode -- which the function's own comment declares the same rule -- give different answers.
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.py:1122-1134: `if two_zone_mode in (ON, DEFAULT): True / elif == OFF: False / else: any(zone key in config)`. The three arms take all three values of const.TWO_ZONE_MODES between them, so the presence rule above them in the comment (`auto ... is the presence rule unchanged; an unknown value is treated as auto`) cannot run for a valid entry. An install that never chose a mode and stores no zone keys -- every single-zone house set up before the mode key, and tests/profiles.py's `house(two_zone=False)` -- is simulated, planned and identified as two zones with the default zone parameters. config_flow._single_zone takes its answer from the same call, so the options flow hides the whole-house loss field on those entries too.

evidence.unit: configs of 6 on which `no mode key` or `auto` answers two_zone_enabled differently from an unknown mode on the same config (no zone keys, and a stored single-zone house: True against False; with zone keys both say True)
evidence.machine: Apple M1 (8 cores), Darwin 27.2.0 arm64, Python 3.14.7 (venv-ci)
evidence.contention_note: shared box during the fan-out, load1 150-270; the number is a static or behavioural count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: the classmethod re-executed in memory with `(const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, const.DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)` replaced by `(const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON,)` (m6_two_zone_auto.py --perturb); the static twin: m6_stmt.py's exhausted_else row for thermal_model.py leaves the census

findings.metric_definition: configs (zone keys absent, present, or a stored single-zone house) x (no mode key, auto) whose two_zone_enabled differs from the same config under an unknown mode string
findings.phenomenon_property: An if/elif chain over one subject whose arms take every value of the enumeration it tests has no further arm carrying logic: an `else` that holds a rule is reachable by a valid value, or the rule is not in force.

null_control.note: the explicit modes are untouched on all three configs (on -> True, off -> False), and with zone keys present the default mode and the unknown mode agree (2 of 2)

findings.proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py: `auto` falls through to the presence rule (the membership test names ON alone). Every golden and scenario built on a config with no zone keys moves back to one zone.
expected_golden_drift: every fixture whose config has no zone keys and no explicit mode: it is two-zone in this tree and single-zone after the fix
